The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

All information about the reference `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

Only one of those characters can make a whole line dashed, so this feature "spreads". The rationale behind this is that you only have to change one character to switch from normal to dashed line, and vice versa. Example: ``` ----+ /----\ +----+ : | | : | | | | |{s} | v \-=--+ +----+ ``` ![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/dashed_demo.png) #### Point markers If `*` is encountered on a line (but not at the end of the line), it is rendered as a special marker, called the point marker. Example: ``` *----* | | /--* * * | | | -*--+ *----* ``` ![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/point_marker.png) #### Text handling If the pattern ' o XXXXX' is encountered, where XXXXX is any text, the 'o' is interpreted and rendered as a bullet point. Note that there must be a space before the 'o' as well as after it. Example: ``` /-----------------\ | Things to do | | cGRE | | o Cut the grass | | o Buy jam | | o Fix car | | o Make website | \-----------------/ ``` ![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/bullet.png) #### HTML mode When `ditaa` is run using the `--html` option, the input is an HTML file. The contents of the `

### Syntax

#### Recognized shapes

The following shapes are recognized by `ditaa`:

- **Document** `{d}`: A shape with a wavy bottom edge
- **Storage** `{s}`: A cylindrical shape (database-like)
- **Ellipse** `{o}`: An oval/ellipse shape
- **Manual operation** `{mo}`: A shape with a slanted top
- **Decision** `{c}` ("Choice"): A diamond shape
- **Trapezoid** `{tr}`: A trapezoid shape
- **Input/Output** `{io}`: A parallelogram shape

Example:

```
+--------+   
|{d}     |   
|        |   
+--------+   
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/document.png)

#### Color

`ditaa` recognizes color codes:

- `cRED` - Red
- `cGRE` - Green
- `cBLU` - Blue
- `cPNK` - Pink
- `cYEL` - Yellow
- `cBLK` - Black

Example:

```
+---------+
| cBLU    |
|         |
|    +----+
|    |cPNK|
|    |    |
+----+----+
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/color.png)

Common edge separation (default):

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/separation.png)

No separation (with the `-E` option):

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/no_separation.png)

#### Dashed lines

Any lines that contain either at least one `=` (for horizontal lines) or at least one `:` (for vertical lines) are rendered as dashed lines. Only one of those characters can make a whole line dashed, so this feature "spreads". The rationale behind this is that you only have to change one character to switch from normal to dashed line, and vice versa.

Example:

```
----+  /----\  +----+
    :  |    |  :    |
    |  |    |  |{s} |
    v  \-=--+  +----+
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/dashed_demo.png)

#### Point markers

If `*` is encountered on a line (but not at the end of the line), it is rendered as a special marker, called the point marker. Example:

```
*----*
|    |      /--*
*    *      |
|    |  -*--+
*----*
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/point_marker.png)

#### Text handling

If the pattern ' o XXXXX' is encountered, where XXXXX is any text, the 'o' is interpreted and rendered as a bullet point. Note that there must be a space before the 'o' as well as after it.

Example:

```
/-----------------\
| Things to do    |
| cGRE            |
| o Cut the grass |
| o Buy jam       |
| o Fix car       |
| o Make website  |
\-----------------/
```

![](https://rawgit.com/stathissideris/ditaa/master/doc/images/bullet.png)

#### HTML mode

When `ditaa` is run using the `--html` option, the input is an HTML file. The contents of the `
` tags are rendered as diagrams and saved in the images directory and a new HTML file is produced with the appropriate `` tags.

If the id parameter is present in the `
` tag, its value is used as the filename of the rendered png. Otherwise a filename of the form `ditaa_diagram_X.png` is used, where X is a number.

In this mode, files that exist are not generated again, they are just skipped. You can force overwrite of the files using the `--overwrite` option.

            with open(os.path.join(d,k),mode) as f: f.write(v)
    r=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    extra=[f for f in sorted(os.listdir(d)) if f not in (files or {})]
    info=[]
    for f in extra:
        p=os.path.join(d,f)
        if os.path.isdir(p):
            info.append(f+"/:"+",".join(sorted(os.listdir(p))))

    if out.startswith("usage:"):

import subprocess, os, shutil, struct, hashlib

def run(args, files=None, stdin=b""):

    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    if files:
        for k,v in files.items():
            pp=os.path.join(d,k)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(pp), exist_ok=True) if os.path.dirname(k) else None
            mode='wb' if isinstance(v,bytes) else 'w'
            with open(pp,mode) as f: f.write(v)
    r=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, cwd=d, input=stdin, capture_output=True)
    out=r.stdout
    err=r.stderr
    extra=[]
    for root,dirs,fs in os.walk(d):
        for fn in fs:
            rel=os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root,fn),d)
            if rel not in (files or {}):
                p=os.path.join(root,fn); data=open(p,'rb').read()
                wh=""
                if data[:8]==b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' and len(data)>=24:
                    w,hh=struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24]); wh=f"{w}x{hh} ct={data[25]}"
                extra.append(f"{rel}({len(data)},{hashlib.md5(data).hexdigest()[:8]},{wh})")
    # summarize stdout
    try:
        outs=out.decode()
        if outs.startswith("usage:"): outs="<usage>"
    except:
        outs=f"<binary {len(out)} md5={hashlib.md5(out).hexdigest()[:8]} head={out[:20]!r}>"
        # if prefix text then binary?
        # try split
    print(f"{args!r} stdin={stdin!r} exit={r.returncode} out={outs!r} err={err.decode(errors='replace')!r} new={extra}")
    return r,d

def svg(content, args=[], name="a.txt", stdin=None):
    # convenience: run svg and print svg output file
    d="/tmp/testrun"
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    if stdin is None:
        with open(os.path.join(d,name),'wb') as f: f.write(content if isinstance(content,bytes) else content.encode())
        argv=[EXE,name,"--svg"]+args
        inp=b""
    else:
        argv=[EXE,"-","-","--svg"]+args
        inp=content if isinstance(content,bytes) else content.encode()
    r=subprocess.run(argv, cwd=d, input=inp, capture_output=True)
    print(f"INPUT:\n{content if isinstance(content,str) else content!r}\nARGS {args} exit={r.returncode} err={r.stderr.decode()!r} out={r.stdout.decode(errors='replace') if stdin is None else '<see below>'}")
    if stdin is not None:
        print("STDOUT:\n", r.stdout.decode(errors='replace'))
    else:
        for f in sorted(os.listdir(d)):
            if f.endswith('.svg'):
                print(open(os.path.join(d,f)).read())
    print("----")
    return r

import subprocess, os, shutil, re
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def svg(content, args=[]):
    d="/tmp/testrun"; shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    open(os.path.join(d,"a.txt"),'wb').write(content if isinstance(content,bytes) else content.encode())
    r=subprocess.run([EXE,"a.txt","--svg"]+args,cwd=d,capture_output=True)
    p=os.path.join(d,"a.svg")
    txt=open(p).read() if os.path.exists(p) else ""
    body=[]
    for line in txt.splitlines():
        line=line.strip()
        if line.startswith(("<path","<text","<rect","<ellipse","<circle","<line","<polygon","<polyline")):
            body.append(line)
    wh=re.search(r"width='([^']*)'\s+height='([^']*)'",txt,re.S)
    print(f"IN {content!r} ARGS {args} exit={r.returncode} size={wh.groups() if wh else None} err={r.stderr.decode()[:200]!r}")
    for b in body: print(" ",b)
    if not os.path.exists(p): print(" NO SVG out=",r.stdout.decode())
    return txt

import zlib, struct
def read_png(path):
    d=open(path,'rb').read()
    pos=8; idat=b''; w=h=None; bit=None; ct=None; palette=None; trns=None
    while pos<len(d):
        ln=struct.unpack('>I',d[pos:pos+4])[0]; typ=d[pos+4:pos+8]; data=d[pos+8:pos+8+ln]; pos+=12+ln
        if typ==b'IHDR': w,h,bit,ct=struct.unpack('>IIBB',data[:10])
        elif typ==b'IDAT': idat+=data
        elif typ==b'PLTE': palette=data
    raw=zlib.decompress(idat)
    # channels
    ch={0:1,2:3,3:1,4:2,6:4}[ct]
    bpp=ch*bit//8
    stride=w*bpp
    out=bytearray(h*stride)
    prev=bytearray(stride)
    p=0
    for y in range(h):
        f=raw[p]; p+=1
        line=bytearray(raw[p:p+stride]); p+=stride
        if f==1:
            for i in range(bpp,stride): line[i]=(line[i]+line[i-bpp])&255
        elif f==2:
            for i in range(stride): line[i]=(line[i]+prev[i])&255
        elif f==3:
            for i in range(stride):
                a=line[i-bpp] if i>=bpp else 0
                line[i]=(line[i]+((a+prev[i])//2))&255
        elif f==4:
            for i in range(stride):
                a=line[i-bpp] if i>=bpp else 0; b=prev[i]; c=prev[i-bpp] if i>=bpp else 0
                pp=a+b-c; pa=abs(pp-a); pb=abs(pp-b); pc=abs(pp-c)
                pr=a if (pa<=pb and pa<=pc) else (b if pb<=pc else c)
                line[i]=(line[i]+pr)&255
        out[y*stride:(y+1)*stride]=line; prev=line
    return w,h,ct,bpp,out
def bbox(path, predicate=None):
    w,h,ct,bpp,pix=read_png(path)
    pts=[]
    for y in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            off=(y*w+x)*bpp
            vals=tuple(pix[off:off+bpp])
            if predicate(vals): pts.append((x,y,vals))
    if not pts: return None
    xs=[p[0] for p in pts]; ys=[p[1] for p in pts]
    return (min(xs),min(ys),max(xs),max(ys),len(pts))

    classes=os.path.join(build,"classes")

import subprocess,os,shutil
def run(exe,args,files):
    d="/tmp/cmp_run"; shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    for k,v in files.items():
        p=os.path.join(d,k)
        if '/' in k: os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True)
        open(p,'w').write(v)
    r=subprocess.run([exe]+args,cwd=d,capture_output=True)
    fl=[]
    for root,dirs,fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs: fl.append(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root,f),d))
    return r,sorted(fl)
cases=[
 (["dir/a.txt"],{"dir/a.txt":"hi\n"}),
 (["dir/a.txt"],{"dir/a.txt":"hi\n","dir/a.png":"x"}),
 (["./a.txt"],{"a.txt":"hi\n"}),
 (["a.b.c.txt"],{"a.b.c.txt":"hi\n"}),
 (["a."],{"a.":"hi\n"}),
 ([".txt"],{".txt":"hi\n"}),
 (["a"],{"a":"hi\n"}),
 (["a.txt"],{ "a.txt":"hi\n", **{f"a_{i}.png":"x" for i in range(2,12)}, "a.png":"x"}),
 (["a.txt","--svg"],{"a.txt":"hi\n","a.svg":"x","a_2.svg":"y"}),
 (["dir/../a.txt"],{"a.txt":"hi\n","dir/x":"y"}),
]
for args,files in cases:
    r1,f1=run("/workspace/executable",args,files); r2,f2=run("/tmp/our_exe",args,files)
    ok=r1.returncode==r2.returncode and r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and f1==f2
    print("OK " if ok else "FAIL",args)
    if not ok:
        print(" ref out",r1.stdout,"files",f1); print(" our out",r2.stdout,"files",f2); print(" err",r1.stderr,r2.stderr)

#!/bin/sh
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
BUILD_DIR=".build"
rm -rf "$BUILD_DIR"
